references.section: Category one and category two businesses
references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Standard 3.2.2A applies to food service, catering and related retail businesses that handle unpackaged, potentially hazardous, ready-to-eat food. Category one businesses (which make such food into ready-to-eat meals) need a food safety supervisor, trained food handlers and records of key food safety controls. Category two businesses (which handle such food unpackaged but don't make it) need a food safety supervisor and trained food handlers.
references.interpretation: Food service businesses need a food safety supervisor and trained food handlers; those that prepare meals also keep records. The page says December 2023 for the start date. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

references.extracted_text: [Summary, not the source's wording] Most food businesses need a food business licence from their local council, including businesses that make food by combining ingredients and businesses that sell unpackaged food by retail, such as cafes, restaurants and takeaways. A licence is not needed if the business only sells unpackaged snack food without cream or custard, whole fruit or vegetables, drinks other than juice made at the point of sale, ice, coffee beans, tea or spices, or primary produce made under a Safe Food Production Queensland accreditation. Every licensable food business must have a food safety supervisor and tell council within 30 days of the licence being issued.
references.interpretation: Making food or selling unpackaged food needs a council licence unless every item is on the exemption list. Selling only pre-packaged food is not making food or selling unpackaged food, so no licence is identified for it. Captured on 2026-10-09 from a reading of the published page; the exact wording was not copied. Replace this with the source's own text, capture a snapshot and verify before relying on it.

You also need a food safety supervisor.
